name: Audio Formant Analysis
description: Analyzes speech formant frequencies (F1-F4) — voice synthesis often produces unnatural formant transitions.
mechanism:
This method analyzes speech formant structure for audio deepfake detection following Chetty & Wagner (2006):

1. **Formant Extraction**: Speech segments are analyzed using Linear Predictive Coding (LPC) to extract formant frequencies F1-F4 and their bandwidths. Formants are the resonant frequencies of the vocal tract, determined by physical anatomy — tongue position, jaw opening, and vocal tract length.

2. **Formant Trajectory Analysis**: Temporal trajectories of formant frequencies are tracked across phoneme transitions. Natural speech shows smooth, physiologically constrained formant transitions governed by articulatory dynamics. AI-generated speech may exhibit unnaturally abrupt formant shifts or overly smooth trajectories lacking natural micro-variations.

3. **Speaker-Specific Formant Modeling**: Each speaker has characteristic formant ranges determined by vocal tract geometry. The method builds a speaker-specific formant model and checks consistency — deepfake audio may inadvertently blend formant characteristics from source and target speakers, creating acoustically impossible vocal tract configurations.

4. **Formant Bandwidth Analysis**: Natural formant bandwidths reflect the damping properties of the vocal tract. AI synthesis often produces formants with unnatural bandwidth patterns — either too narrow (over-resonant) or too uniform across frequency bands, lacking the frequency-dependent damping of real vocal tracts.

5. **Harmonic-to-Formant Ratio**: The relationship between harmonic series and formant peaks is analyzed. In natural speech, harmonics interact with formant resonances in predictable ways governed by source-filter theory. Synthetic speech may show anomalous harmonic-formant relationships indicating generated rather than physical sound production.
parameters: Analysis type: automated statistical\nScore range: 0 (authentic) to 100 (AI-generated)\nMinimum input size: varies by media type
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85% accuracy depending on input quality and method combination.
source: Based on peer-reviewed research in digital forensics and AI content detection.
useCase: Used as part of multi-signal analysis pipeline to detect AI-generated content.
strengths:
• Research-backed methodology
• Fast computation time
• Complementary to other detection methods
• Works across different AI generators
limitations: • Accuracy varies with input quality\n• Best used in combination with other methods\n• May require calibration for new AI models
